rubric.question: Which queue should handle this ticket?
Policy: any refund above 5000 needs manager approval. Does this ticket need one?
Is there a risk of chargeback, churn, or public escalation?

options.description: Yes, the ticket signals escalation risk

rubric.question: Assess the claim: the customer has already contacted support about this.
Is there enough information in the ticket to act on it?
Should the first reply come from a person or an automated acknowledgement?
Does the customer state a deadline or time limit?
Is the customer asking for money back rather than a fix?

tickets.label: Double charge, threatening a dispute
tickets.text:
Ticket #4471 — Priya R.

I was charged twice for order A-9923 on 14 March. Both charges show on my card statement, 4,860 each, and I have attached screenshots of both. I emailed on the 15th and again on the 18th and nobody has replied.

I need one of these charges reversed. If I don't hear back by tomorrow I am raising a dispute with my bank and I will be posting about this.

tickets.label: Locked out before a deadline
tickets.text:
Ticket #4488 — Daniel O.

Hi, I can't sign in to my account. I have asked for a password reset four times today and the email never arrives — I checked spam. My team's quarterly report is due Friday and everything is in there.

Is there another way to verify who I am? Happy to jump on a call. Thanks for any help.

tickets.label: Parcel missing, first contact
tickets.text:
Ticket #4502 — Anu K.

Order B-1180 was marked delivered on Monday but nothing arrived. The tracking says it left the depot on Saturday. I've checked with the neighbours and the building reception, no one has it.

This is the first time I'm writing in. Could you look into where it went? I'd rather have the item than a refund if it can still be found.
